The citation network of History PhDs

5,631 History PhDs and the 11,411 works they most often cite, joined by 153,757 citations and laid out so that theses citing the same literature sit together (a force-directed layout of the ForceAtlas2 kind). Theses are coloured by where the degree was awarded; works are dark and sized by how many of the drawn theses cite them.

How to read this

  • What is drawn. Strict History PhDs (7,107 in the graph) and every work cited by at least 8 of them, or by at least 4 within France, the rest of Europe or elsewhere, so the smaller regions' own canons are drawn too. 1,476 theses cite none of these works and are not drawn; most are European, where citation is more dispersed.
  • Position. Linked nodes attract and all nodes repel, so a thesis sits among the works it cites and a work among the theses citing it. Distance across the map is only meaningful as clustering; the axes have no meaning.
  • Works are first-author surname and main title; translations mapped through Wikidata count as one work. A citation is not engagement.

Built 2026-10-23 (scripts/network_layout.py, scripts/render_network_page.py). See also the map of the most cited works, Europe, Canada and the United States and Canada and the United States.
